sections.title: How the sky becomes a chart
sections.blurb: What a natal chart is, and the grammar of reading one.

blocks.text: HOW THE SKY BECOMES A CHART

A natal chart is not a fortune. It is a map of where ten bodies stood, seen from the exact spot on Earth where you were born, at the minute you arrived. Seven were named by the ancients; three are modern receptions, said so wherever they appear. Here is how that map is drawn, and how five ancient cultures learned to read it.
ONE · THE VIEW FROM EARTH
The signs are constellations

Look up from anywhere. The Sun, the Moon, and the planets visible to the naked eye all drift along a single narrow band of sky. Behind that band sits a ring of constellations. Ancient observers cut the ring into twelve equal arcs of thirty degrees and named them: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and the rest.

Those twelve arcs are the signs. A planet is "in" a sign when, from where you stand on Earth, it sits in front of that stretch of the ring. The signs hold still. The planets are the wanderers that cross them.
TWO · A WORKED EXAMPLE
This is a chart

Drawn at fixed positions so the structure is clear. The outer ring is the zodiac. Each glyph is one of the ten bodies. The lines between them are aspects: bone where the forces ease one another, rose where they pull against.
THREE · THE GRAMMAR
The planets are verbs. The signs say how.

There is a simple grammar under all of it. A planet is the verb, the thing being done. A sign is the manner, the way it is done. The house, which you meet next, is the room it is done in. Put them together and a placement becomes a sentence.

So Mars in Aries reads "I act, boldly and first." Add the house and you have where: in the Tenth, that drive is spent on your public standing. Every culture on this site reads the same computed sky; what changes is the theology it must pass through. Mars becomes Resheph in Canaan, Ares in Greece, Mars Pater in Rome, and the sentence still holds.
FOUR · THE TURNING SKY
The rising horizon

The hour and the place matter because they fix the horizon. The sign climbing the eastern horizon at your birth is your Ascendant, the start of your First House. The sign setting in the west sits opposite. Two people born the same day, hours apart, do not share a chart: the sky has turned beneath them.
FIVE · THE TWELVE FIELDS
The houses

From the Ascendant, the sky is divided into twelve fields called houses, each a department of life: the body, what you own, kin, home, pleasure, work, partnership, and so on. A planet's sign says how it acts; its house says where in your life that force is spent.

Astra Antiqua uses whole-sign houses, the oldest Hellenistic system: the rising sign becomes the entire First House, and each sign after it the next in order. It is the historically correct choice for an ancient system, and it stays meaningful even when the birth hour is only approximate.
SIX · FROM ASTRONOMY TO MEANING
Where astrology begins

Everything to this point is astronomy no observatory would dispute: real bodies in real positions, computed to the arcminute. Astrology is the interpretive layer laid on top, the old agreement that these positions carry meaning.

We do not invent that layer. We borrow it from the people who built it: the priests of Memphis, the oracle at Delphi, the scribes of Ugarit, the suffetes of Carthage, the augurs of Rome. The same Mars at the same degree is read five different ways, and you choose whose voice to read it in.
Now draw yours.

Set the date, the hour, and the place of your birth. The ten bodies will be placed for the exact moment you arrived, your houses raised from the rising sign, and the whole thing read in whichever ancient voice you call on.

sections.blurb: The twelve signs, their dates, and their tempers.

blocks.text: ZODIAC SUN SIGNS

The part of astrology almost everyone already knows. When you say "I am a Leo," you mean the Sun stood in Leo at the hour of your birth. Because the Earth circles the Sun once a year, the Sun walks through all twelve signs in the same order every year, so the dates barely move. Astra Antiqua uses the tropical zodiac, anchored to the seasons rather than to the slowly drifting constellations.

sections.title: The rising sign
sections.blurb: The Ascendant, and why it turns about every two hours.

blocks.text: THE RISING SIGN, OR ASCENDANT

The rising sign, or Ascendant, is the zodiac sign that was climbing the eastern horizon at the hour and place you were born. It is the cusp of your First House, and the point from which all your other houses are raised. Where your Sun sign answers "what," the rising sign answers "how you arrive": the face you lead with.
ONE · IT MOVES FAST
It changes every two hours

Across a day the whole zodiac appears to wheel past the horizon. The signs are not moving around us; the Earth is turning, a full three hundred and sixty degrees every twenty-four hours. Divide that by twelve and a new sign climbs the eastern horizon roughly every two hours. This is why the rising sign needs your birth time, not just your birth date.
TWO · TWO MOTIONS
The orbit and the spin
Two motions happen at once. The Earth orbits the Sun, one full revolution a year. The Earth also rotates on its own axis, one full turn a day.

Your planet signs, your Sun in Scorpio, your Mercury in Aquarius, come from the slow yearly orbit: they say which stretch of the zodiac each planet stood in front of. Your rising sign comes from the fast daily spin: it says which stretch was on your eastern horizon at that exact minute. The first changes over weeks. The second changes every couple of hours.
THREE · SAME HOUR, FAR APART
Two births, opposite sides

Imagine two people born at the very same instant, but on opposite sides of the Earth. Their planet signs are nearly identical: from either place, the planets sit in front of the same far constellations.

What changes is their horizon, literally what each of them sees to the east. Standing on opposite faces of a turning globe, they look out at different parts of the zodiac. Same charts, different risings. It is the one piece of the chart that is truly local to you.
Find your rising sign.
Because it turns on the minute and the place, you need your birth time and city. Enter them and the Ascendant, and the twelve houses raised from it, will be computed for the exact moment you arrived.

sections.title: The houses
sections.blurb: The twelve fields of life the planets fall into.

blocks.text: THE TWELVE HOUSES

If the signs are how a planet acts and the planets are what is acting, the houses are where it acts. They are the twelve fields of life, raised from the sign rising at your birth: the body, what you own, kin, home, pleasure, work, partnership, and so on around the wheel. A planet's house tells you which corner of your life its force is spent in.
Astra Antiqua raises these with whole-sign houses, where the rising sign becomes the entire First House and each sign after it the next. For how that compares to other methods, see house systems .

sections.title: House systems
sections.blurb: Different ways to cut the sky into twelve, and the one we use.

blocks.text: HOUSE SYSTEMS

Everyone agrees on where the planets are. Astrologers do not always agree on how to slice the sky into twelve houses. The planet positions stay the same; the house a planet lands in can shift depending on the method. Here are the three you are most likely to meet.
OUR CHOICE
Why we use whole-sign

For an app that reads the sky the way the ancients did, whole-sign is the honest choice: it is the system the Hellenistic astrologers actually used, the one Egypt, Greece, Canaan, Carthage, and Rome would all recognize.

It also fails gracefully. The time-based systems need your birth minute to be exact; a half-hour error can push a planet into the wrong house. Whole-sign only needs the rising sign, so an approximate birth time still gives a sound chart. Real ancient method, and steadier when the records are imperfect.

sections.title: Transits and orbs
sections.blurb: How today's sky touches your birth chart, and how close counts.

blocks.text: TRANSITS AND ORBS

Your natal chart is frozen at the minute of your birth. The sky is not. Since you were born the planets have kept moving, and a transit is what happens when one of them, where it is right now, makes an aspect to where a planet stood in your birth chart. It is how astrology marks the seasons of a life.
ONE · THE CLOCK OF THE SKY
Fast planets, slow planets

Each planet keeps its own clock. The Sun rounds the zodiac once a year, so it makes a big transit to itself about every three months: a conjunction on your birthday (your solar return), a square three months later, an opposition at the half-year.

Saturn takes about twenty-nine years to return to where it began, which is why the much-discussed Saturn return lands near ages twenty-nine, fifty-eight, and eighty-seven, each one a reckoning with responsibility. Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto move slower still; their transits are rare enough to mark whole chapters, not seasons.
TWO · HOW CLOSE COUNTS
The orb

A transit is rarely exact to the degree, and it would be useless if it only counted at the precise instant. An orb is the buffer around an angle: the margin within which we still call it an aspect. Astra Antiqua runs one documented orb table everywhere on this site, natal, transit, and synastry alike. Nothing is estimated and nothing is widened to manufacture a reading; when nothing sits inside these margins, the day is quiet.
The closer a transit is to exact, the louder it is meant to read.
Transits run through the whole app

Your daily reading is built from the transits touching your chart today. The long transits and the year-ahead forecast track every major transit, eclipse, retrograde, and your solar return for the next twelve months, each timed to the day.

houseSystems.name: Whole Sign
houseSystems.body: The oldest method, and the one Hellenistic astrologers used for roughly a thousand years. The entire sign rising on the Ascendant becomes the First House; the next sign is the Second, and so on. Every house is exactly thirty degrees. It is simple to compute, and quirks like intercepted signs cannot occur.

houseSystems.name: Placidus
houseSystems.body: A time-based method. The cusps are marked in two-hour steps from your birth: the degree rising at birth is the First House cusp, then where that degree has moved about two hours later is the next, and so on. Because signs spend unequal time on the horizon, the houses come out unequal, more so the farther from the equator you were born.

houseSystems.name: Porphyry
houseSystems.body: Prioritizes the four angles. The Ascendant and Midheaven are computed exactly and become the First and Tenth cusps; the arc between each pair of angles is then split into three equal parts for the houses in between. A middle path between equal and time-based systems.

egypt.conjunction: Two gods ride in one barque. Where the river carries it, it carries them both.
egypt.sextile: A fair wind stands on the river. It moves only the boat that raises a sail.
egypt.square: Isfet crossed the threshold of the hall. The pans come level again through labor, and the labor is yours.
egypt.trine: Heart and feather agree and no hand touches the scale. Go on with the day; the hall asks you nothing.
egypt.opposition: The two pans hang level, and neither falls. The scribe writes no verdict until one side descends.

greece.conjunction: The tripod answers once for two gods. Nothing in the answer belongs to one more than the other.
greece.sextile: The shrine takes questions today. An unasked god has nothing to say to you.
greece.square: The price is named before the answer, and it is not small. Pay it, or ask nothing.
greece.trine: The oracle speaks before the question is finished. The god volunteered the answer.
greece.opposition: Delphi says one thing and Dodona the other. Both answers are true, and acting on one breaks the other.

canaan.conjunction: The docket carries two names under a single heading. Whatever El decrees falls on the pair.
canaan.sextile: Nothing reaches the council but by vow. Silence keeps the matter off the list.
canaan.square: A witness rises against the matter. Nothing passes at this sitting that is not spoken against first.
canaan.trine: No vow was made and the rains came anyway. The wadis are running full.
canaan.opposition: Baal holds above and Mot holds below. El hears both and decrees nothing.

carthage.conjunction: One manifest covers two cargoes. Profit or loss, the ledger no longer tells them apart.
carthage.sextile: The harbor is open and a berth is held in your name. Nothing loads itself.
carthage.square: Short weight turns up in the audit. Trade goes on, and a clerk watches every measure you make.
carthage.trine: The sailing season opens and the ledger is clean. Nothing stands against your name in the precinct.
carthage.opposition: Two merchants claim one cargo at the quay. The hold stays sealed and the season runs on without it.

rome.conjunction: The auspice was taken once and it binds two names. Neither can act on it alone.
rome.sextile: The birds are favorable and no one has yet taken the auspice. A sign unclaimed confers no right to act.
rome.square: An objection is entered and the objector has standing. Every step of this goes forward under challenge.
rome.trine: The day stands fastus and the augury attached no condition. What is done under it holds.
rome.opposition: Two magistrates, one office. Each vetoes the other, and the day's business stands adjourned.

aspectGeometry.conjunction: Same point in the sky; the two forces fuse and read as one.
aspectGeometry.sextile: Sixty degrees apart, a third of a square; an opening, not a guarantee.
aspectGeometry.square: Ninety degrees apart, a right angle; friction, and a forced choice.
aspectGeometry.trine: A hundred twenty degrees, a third of the circle; the easiest geometry there is.
aspectGeometry.opposition: A hundred eighty degrees, the two ends of one line; a mirror, not an enemy.
